name: Milk (cow)
description: The daily glass, chai base, and kheer canvas.

tcm.note: Neutral-moistening; TCM uses it for dryness.

ayurveda.note: The classic cooling, building food — warm milk is still shita-virya.

unani.note: Doodh is thanda-tar; hence warming additions like haldi or saffron.

histamine.note: Fresh pasteurized milk is low; the aged/fermented dairy family is where trouble starts.

name: Yogurt
description: Cultured milk — and the traditions' most famous disagreement.

tcm.note: Thinly classified; modern TCM leans cool-damp.

ayurveda.note: The classic surprise: dahi is USHNA (sour, channel-clogging) — avoid at night.

unani.note: Dahi is textbook thanda in desi/Unani usage — the exact opposite of Ayurveda.

histamine.note: Fermented but young; fine for many, borderline for the very sensitive.

name: Buttermilk (chaas)
description: Thin churned yogurt drink, salted and spiced.

tcm.note: Not classical.

ayurveda.note: Takra is milder than dahi — praised as digestive; schools call it mildly heating yet pitta-manageable.

unani.note: Chaas/ayran is the everyday summer cooler.

histamine.note: As yogurt.

name: Paneer
description: Fresh unaged pressed cheese of palak paneer.

tcm.note: Not classical.

ayurveda.note: Fresh cheese = heavy, building, cooling-leaning.

histamine.note: Fresh unaged cheese — far safer than aged.

name: Ghee
description: Clarified butter — sacred fat of two traditions.

tcm.note: Fats read warming in TCM.

ayurveda.note: The famous answer: ghee is SHITA-virya — cooling, pitta's best fat.

unani.note: Desi folk calls ghee garam — another clean tradition split.

histamine.note: Milk solids removed — the safest dairy fat.

name: Butter
description: Everyday dairy fat.

tcm.note: Thin classical documentation.

ayurveda.note: Fresh makkhan is cooling-building.

unani.note: Some hakims group it with ghee (garam), others call fresh makkhan cool.

histamine.note: Well tolerated; minimal protein.

name: Cream
description: Rich milk fat of qorma and qishta desserts.

ayurveda.note: Heavy-building like milk.

unani.note: Malai follows milk's thanda nature.

histamine.note: Fresh cream low; whipped/aged products vary.

name: Fresh cheese (mozzarella/akkawi)
description: Young white cheeses — pizza's stretch and kunafa's heart.

tcm.note: Not classical.

ayurveda.note: As fresh cheese.

histamine.note: Young cheeses are the tolerable end of cheese.

name: Aged cheese
description: Matured hard cheeses — flavor built by the very aging that builds histamine.

tcm.note: Not classical; rich-aged foods lean warm.

ayurveda.note: Aged + sour = heating, tamasic.

unani.note: Aged jibn leans garam in Unani sources.

histamine.note: The textbook high-histamine food — months of aging = maximal amines.

name: Labneh
description: Thick strained yogurt eaten with zaatar and oil.

tcm.note: Not classical.

ayurveda.note: Follows dahi (sour, concentrated).

unani.note: Follows laban's cooling nature in Arab usage.

histamine.note: As yogurt, slightly concentrated.

name: Ice cream
description: Frozen sweet cream — physically cold, energetically argued over.

tcm.note: TCM warns cold-damp foods 'injure the spleen' — cooling but not recommended for it.

ayurveda.note: Cooling but heavy and ama-forming.

histamine.note: Base is modest; chocolate/strawberry flavors inherit those triggers.

name: Greek yogurt
description: Yogurt with the whey strained out — thicker, and double the protein.

tcm.note: Follows plain yogurt; straining removes water, not nature.

ayurveda.note: Dahi is ushna whatever you strain out of it.

unani.note: Thanda like dahi, though less watery than the desi original.

histamine.note: Young culture, like plain yogurt — the aged cheeses are the problem, not this.

nutrition.highlight: double the protein of plain yogurt

name: Feta
description: Salty brined white cheese, crumbled over everything from salad to eggs.

tcm.note: Brined cheese is not a classical TCM entry; placed by analogy to fresh dairy.

ayurveda.note: Sour plus salty plus fermented reads ushna, unlike fresh paneer.

unani.note: Salt and ripening push it toward garam; the classical texts describe fresh cheese, not this.

histamine.note: Brine-ripened, so well above fresh cheese — though below a hard aged block.

name: Halloumi
description: The cheese that grills instead of melting — squeaky, salty, Levantine.

tcm.note: Outside the classical record; treated as fresh dairy.

ayurveda.note: Salt-cured and usually cooked over direct heat.

unani.note: Salting dries it; grilling adds to that.

histamine.note: Unripened despite the salt — closer to paneer than to feta on the SIGHI list.

nutrition.highlight: holds its shape on a grill

name: Cottage cheese
description: Loose fresh curds, barely cultured — the plainest cheese there is.

tcm.note: Fresh dairy, neutral and moistening.

ayurveda.note: Fresh unsoured curd stays shita — it is souring that turns dairy ushna.

unani.note: Thanda-tar, the same reading as paneer.

histamine.note: Fresh and lightly cultured; among the safer cheeses for a reactive day.

name: Ricotta
description: Soft, sweet-tasting cheese made from the whey another cheese left behind.

tcm.note: Not classically classified; read as fresh dairy.

ayurveda.note: Fresh and unsoured, so shita like other unfermented curds.

unani.note: Placed with the fresh cheeses.

histamine.note: Fresh, but spoils fast — age is what moves cheese up this scale.

name: Cream cheese
description: Spreadable fresh cheese, rich enough to be mostly fat.

tcm.note: Modern product; read as rich fresh dairy, which TCM calls damp-forming.

ayurveda.note: Fresh and unsoured, so shita — but very guru, heavy and slow.

unani.note: Cold and wet like the fresh cheeses it belongs with.

histamine.note: Fresh; the flavoured tubs inherit whatever is stirred into them.

name: Processed cheese
description: Aged cheese melted down with emulsifiers into slices and tubs.

tcm.note: Inherits from the aged cheese it is built out of.

ayurveda.note: An aged base, so ushna, however mild it tastes.

unani.note: Garam by inheritance; no classical entry exists for a processed slice.

histamine.note: Built from ripened cheese, so it carries ripened-cheese histamine — the mild taste hides it.

name: Sour cream
description: Cream soured with cultures — the cooling spoon on a hot plate.

tcm.note: Read with the cultured dairy family.

ayurveda.note: Soured dairy is ushna, the same logic that makes dahi heating.

unani.note: Thanda in practice, which is why it is served against chilli heat.

histamine.note: Cultured but young.

name: Kefir
description: Milk fermented with grains into a thin, fizzy, sharply sour drink.

tcm.note: Not a classical food; placed with cultured milk.

ayurveda.note: Strongly soured, so ushna — more so than plain dahi.

unani.note: Read as a thinner, sourer dahi.

histamine.note: A live, mixed, long ferment — the mechanism that makes kefir interesting is also the one that makes histamine.

name: Condensed milk
description: Milk boiled down with sugar until it pours like syrup.

tcm.note: Long reduction concentrates and warms; sweet and damp-forming.

ayurveda.note: Cooked down and heavily sweetened — the cooking is what turns milk's shita.

unani.note: Garam by preparation rather than by ingredient.

histamine.note: Heat-treated and sugar-preserved; low in itself.

name: Evaporated milk
description: Milk with most of its water removed, and no sugar added.

tcm.note: Concentrated milk; the nature of milk is not changed by removing water.

ayurveda.note: Still shita, only heavier — unlike its sweetened cousin.

unani.note: Reads as milk, thickened.

histamine.note: Sterilised in the tin; low.

name: Khoya
description: Milk stirred over heat for hours until only the solids remain — the base of most mithai.

tcm.note: Hours of reduction; TCM reads long-cooked concentrates as warming and damp-forming.

ayurveda.note: Classically milk keeps its shita virya however far you reduce it — it becomes guru, not ushna.

unani.note: Desi hakimi usage is firm that mawa mithai is garam — the opposite of the classical Ayurvedic reading.

histamine.note: Low in itself; the sweets built on it usually add nuts and khoya sits out at room temperature in shops.

name: Buffalo milk
description: The default milk across much of South Asia — thicker and far richer than cow's.

tcm.note: Not a staple of the Chinese record; read alongside cow's milk.

ayurveda.note: Mahisha dugdha is classically shita and guru, and specifically named as sleep-inducing.

unani.note: Thanda and heavy — more so than cow's milk, which is why it is cut with water for chai.

histamine.note: Fresh milk, low — same as cow's.

nutrition.highlight: nearly twice the fat of cow's milk

name: Goat milk
description: Lighter and easier on the stomach than cow's milk, with a distinct tang.

tcm.note: Goat's milk is explicitly warm in TCM, tonifying — unlike cow's milk, which is neutral.

ayurveda.note: Aja dugdha is shita but light and astringent — classically given in fever, where cow's milk is too heavy.

unani.note: Treated as the most temperate of the milks, close to balanced.

histamine.note: Fresh milk; low.

name: Camel milk
description: Gulf staple — thin, faintly salty, and the one milk the traditions call warming.

tcm.note: Absent from the Chinese record; placed by analogy only.

ayurveda.note: Ushtra dugdha is named ushna — light, slightly salty, and the exception among milks.

unani.note: Garam in Arab and Unani usage, given for chest and digestive complaints.

histamine.note: Fresh milk; low. Often sold raw, which is a separate question from histamine.
